instruction: Navigate to the Exceptions topic page on this CS50 Python course.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated CS50 Python course weeks 1-9 sequentially, downloading lecture PDFs from each week page. Files downloaded to Chrome default directory instead of /home/user/lecture_slides/.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome to specific URLs, click PDF links on web pages, navigate through course week pages sequentially, identify and interact with CS50 course website sidebar
metadata.failure_analysis: Model downloaded PDFs to Chrome default Downloads folder instead of the specified /home/user/lecture_slides/ directory. Never attempted to change download location or move files.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original multi-week download task into a single navigation sub-task. Model demonstrated it can navigate to week pages, so this tests that capability in isolation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating from Week 0 to Week 3 (Exceptions) on CS50 Python course. Evaluator checks active tab URL matches the Week 3 pattern.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree, returning a string URL suitable for the metric.
Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly receives the rules dict directly (expected.type='rule') and accesses rules['expected'] to get the list of regex patterns.
CS50 Python Week 3 is indeed the 'Exceptions' topic, so the expected URL pattern 'cs50\.harvard\.edu/python/.*weeks/3' is semantically correct for the instruction.
Single-step navigation task is fully covered by a single URL pattern check — no missing verification steps.

Minor: regex pattern 'weeks/3' lacks a trailing boundary (e.g., 'weeks/3(/|$)'), so it could theoretically match 'weeks/30' etc., but CS50 Python only has weeks 0-9, making this a non-issue in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: tighten regex to 'weeks/3(/|$)' to prevent theoretical false positives on 'weeks/30+' URLs.
